topics.article_title: When Reasoning Does Not Pay: Short Factual Answers
topics.why_it_exists: Quantify whether enabling reasoning_effort improves a task whose answers are short and factual, where there is little to reason about.
topics.storyline_question: If quality is already near-ceiling, does paying for more reasoning buy anything?
observed_patterns: Cost climbs from 0.000663 USD/req (minimal) to 0.005043 USD/req (xhigh) per results/cost-curves/benchmark-01-cost-per-request.csv (~7.6x).
Latency climbs 1112.8 ms (minimal) to 3088.0 ms (xhigh) per results/cost-curves/benchmark-01-latency.csv.
Mean judge score stays within 1.73-1.88 across all cells per results/cost-curves/benchmark-01-quality.csv (no monotonic quality gain).
topics.operator_takeaway: On short factual workloads, escalating reasoning_effort raises cost and latency without a clear quality return; default to minimal/none.
topics.public_safety_notes: PAYG cost lens; pricing cited from pricing/azure-openai-payg-2026-05.yaml; N=20,R=3 so use std not CI.

topics.why_it_exists: Contrast case to T01: a task where intermediate reasoning is load-bearing for correctness.
topics.storyline_question: On a task that actually requires steps, how much quality does even a little reasoning add, and at what cost?
observed_patterns: gpt-4o baseline mean judge score 1.5; gpt-5.2 reaches 2.0 at none/medium/high/xhigh per benchmarks/02-multi-step-reasoning/analysis.json cell_stats.
The 2.0-quality 'high' cell costs 0.00125 USD/req vs 0.000798 for gpt-4o baseline per results/cost-curves/benchmark-02-cost-per-request.csv.
topics.operator_takeaway: On multi-step tasks, a modest reasoning_effort closes a real quality gap; the marginal cost is small relative to the correctness gain.
topics.public_safety_notes: The gpt-5.2 'minimal' cell has n_used=0 (no usable runs) per analysis.json; exclude it from any chart rather than plotting a zero.

topics.why_it_exists: Measure reasoning value when the model must select and call tools (calculator, web_search) rather than answer directly.
topics.storyline_question: When tools already do the heavy lifting, does extra reasoning still help or just add latency?
observed_patterns: Quality is near-saturated (1.85-2.0) across cells per benchmarks/03-tool-using-agent/analysis.json; analysis.json also carries a tool_efficiency_breakdown block.
Latency rises from 2902 ms (none) to 3770 ms (xhigh) per results/cost-curves/benchmark-03-latency.csv while cost stays ~0.0028-0.0035 USD/req.
topics.operator_takeaway: For tool-using agents already near quality ceiling, prefer lower reasoning_effort to keep latency down; reserve higher effort for genuinely hard tool-planning.
topics.public_safety_notes: tool_efficiency_breakdown is an additional chart angle (tool-call efficiency); needs-light-aggregation to chart. The gpt-5.2 'minimal' cell has n_used=0 (no usable runs) per analysis.json; exclude it from any chart.

topics.why_it_exists: Show the billed-but-invisible reasoning tokens that drive the cost gap a per-token price comparison hides.
topics.storyline_question: Where does the extra bill come from when output text barely changes?
observed_patterns: Benchmark 01 mean_reasoning_tokens rises 3.66 (minimal) -> 311.47 (xhigh) while mean_output_tokens only moves 12.67 -> 17.88 per results/token-composition/benchmark-01-tokens.csv.
Reasoning tokens are billed at the output rate (reasoning_per_1m_usd=14.00 == output_per_1m_usd) per pricing/azure-openai-payg-2026-05.yaml.
topics.operator_takeaway: Always capture response.usage reasoning tokens separately; they, not visible output, explain most of the post-migration cost rise.
topics.public_safety_notes: Stacked-bar maps directly to the four token columns already present in each tokens.csv.

topics.article_title: PTU vs PAYG: Where the Lines Cross
topics.why_it_exists: Reasoning tokens consume PTU capacity; teams need a basis to decide between consumption (PAYG) and reserved (PTU) billing.
topics.storyline_question: At what utilization does reserved PTU capacity beat PAYG for a reasoning workload?
observed_patterns: Token-shape throughput-gain factor for benchmark-01 falls from 0.9846 (minimal) to 0.4518 (xhigh) per results/cost-curves/benchmark-01-throughput-gain.csv: at fixed token shape, higher effort serves fewer requests per unit baseline throughput. The factor is baseline.tokens_per_request / target.tokens_per_request (a same-model token-shape proxy), not a cross-model PTU throughput ratio.
PTU density gpt-5.2 = 3400 input TPM/PTU vs gpt-4o = 2500 per pricing/ptu-density-2026-05.yaml.
topics.operator_takeaway: Reasoning effort directly lowers token-shape throughput-per-request; size PTU on reasoning-inclusive token shape, and use scripts/ptu_sizing.py with a measured WorkloadShape (which applies model density).
topics.public_safety_notes: Crossover curve must be computed from the public pricing snapshots + ptu_sizing.py; an explicit USD-vs-throughput crossover CSV does not yet exist (mark crossover line needs-new-chart). Throughput-gain bars are ready.

topics.why_it_exists: Measure how splitting traffic across more prompt_cache_key buckets (and retention mode) affects cache hit ratio and first-token latency.
topics.storyline_question: Does a high-cardinality cache key quietly destroy your cache hit ratio and TTFT?
observed_patterns: in_memory cardinality 1 -> TTFT p95 106389.96 ms vs 24h cardinality 1 -> 9899.74 ms per results/cache-key-bucketing/ttft_p95_vs_cardinality.csv (retention mode dominates TTFT here).
Cache hit ratio stays high (0.9334-0.9612) across the measured cells per results/cache-key-bucketing/cache_hit_ratio_vs_cardinality.csv.
topics.operator_takeaway: Retention mode (24h vs in_memory) drives steady-state TTFT more than cardinality in these cells; keep the cacheable prefix stable and pick retention deliberately.
topics.public_safety_notes: PAYG, not PTU (metadata.ptu_evidence=false). Only 2 cardinality points (1, 8) per retention; label the line as sparse.

topics.article_title: What Retry-After Actually Looks Like on 429s
topics.why_it_exists: Characterize the Retry-After-ms the service returns on 429s so backoff/admission logic can be grounded in observed values.
topics.storyline_question: When you get throttled, how long does the service actually tell you to wait?
observed_patterns: Overall n=193 429s; p50=43.0 ms, p90=50.8 ms, p99=16921.12 ms, max=17258.0 ms per results/retry-after-characterization/retry_after_ms_percentiles.csv (long-tailed).
Two mechanisms differ: task013 burst-driven p50=43.0 ms vs task019 reservation-driven p50=3.0 ms per benchmarks/08-retry-after-characterization/analysis.json by_mechanism.
topics.operator_takeaway: Most Retry-After values are tens of ms but a heavy p99 tail exists; size backoff for the tail, not the median.
topics.public_safety_notes: Single-tenant, source-run-scoped, descriptive only (scope field in analysis.json); not customer-attributed and not direct PTU evidence.

topics.why_it_exists: Compare a proactive admission/spillover policy against a reactive one under burst load across endpoints.
topics.storyline_question: Does spilling proactively recover cache hit ratio / avoid 429s better than reacting after the fact?
observed_patterns: Proactive run observed real_429_count=0 with overall cache_hit_ratio=0.99094 per benchmarks/04-spillover-simulation/analysis.json per_policy_stats.proactive.
Aggregate proactive-minus-reactive cache hit delta is +0.046 percentage points per benchmarks/04-spillover-simulation/analysis.json comparison (near parity in this run).
topics.operator_takeaway: In this simulation the proactive policy avoided 429s entirely while reaching near-identical steady-state cache hit ratio; recovery timelines are the most legible chart.
topics.public_safety_notes: Benchmark 04 is a simulation; benchmark 05 dual-spillover hits real infra but is workload-shaped, not customer-attributed. Time-series CSVs are large (~2-4k rows); downsample for rendering.

topics.why_it_exists: Validate an offline admission-controller model (reserve at admission, leak continuously) against observed 429 timing and Retry-After.
topics.storyline_question: Can a simple leak-rate admission model predict when 429s appear?
observed_patterns: In-sample confusion matrix tp=60, fp=5, fn=107, tn=4267 over n_events=4439 per benchmarks/10-replay-validation/calibration.json (high precision, low recall in-sample).
Fitted k_leak_tokens_per_ptu_per_second=3.9103 per benchmarks/10-replay-validation/calibration.json.
topics.operator_takeaway: A continuous-leak admission model captures some 429 onsets precisely but misses many (high FN); treat it as a planning proxy, not a guarantee.
topics.public_safety_notes: Only PNGs exist for the scatter; the numeric residuals live in calibration.json (no paired CSV). Proxy, not direct PTU-pool observation.

topics.why_it_exists: Probe how max_output_tokens reservation interacts with the throttled PAYG admission layer (proxy for PTU admission reservation).
topics.storyline_question: Does raising max_output_tokens reserve capacity and trigger 429s earlier?
observed_patterns: task019 reservation-driven 429s have a tight Retry-After distribution (p50=3.0 ms, max=60.0 ms) per benchmarks/08-retry-after-characterization/analysis.json by_mechanism.task019_reservation_driven.
topics.operator_takeaway: max_output_tokens is a reservation, not just a cap; on a capacity-bound deployment it can move the 429 onset. Verify on your own deployment.
topics.public_safety_notes: PAYG-throttled proxy, explicitly NOT PTU evidence (analysis.md banner). Smoke-tier runs; chart needs aggregation from the sweep summary JSONs.

topics.article_title: How the Data Is Sanitized: Evidence Gates and Release Tiers
topics.why_it_exists: Explain the SANITIZED_PUBLIC / RAW_PRIVATE / AGGREGATE_AZURE_SAMPLE tiering and the redaction provenance recorded for every published artifact.
topics.storyline_question: How can readers trust that public numbers are faithful yet leak nothing private?
observed_patterns: release/public_sanitized_manifest.json carries one provenance entry per published artifact (sha256, redaction_rules_sha256, tier=SANITIZED_PUBLIC).
topics.operator_takeaway: Reproducible research needs a verifiable redaction boundary; the manifest + sanitizer --verify make the public surface auditable.
topics.public_safety_notes: Meta/methodology topic; uses existing hand-authored SVGs. Do not render any RAW_PRIVATE sample.

topics.why_it_exists: Document the locale set (en, ko, ja, zh-CN, hi), hreflang/canonical metadata, and the stale-translation source-hash gate.
topics.storyline_question: How do you keep five translated pages from silently drifting out of sync?
observed_patterns: docs/validate.sh recomputes the EN <main> source-content sha256 and fails any locale page whose recorded i18n:source-content-sha256 differs (stale-translation gate).
topics.operator_takeaway: A per-page source-content hash turns 'is this translation stale?' into a deterministic CI check.
topics.public_safety_notes: Optional/meta topic; existing SVG and validate.sh only. No data artifacts involved.
